Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call: 

1) Decision criteria we heard
- Low-latency inference for customer-facing features (p95 < 200ms)
- SOC 2 and penetration test evidence required for procurement
- Ability to isolate data and provide audit logs for regulatory review
- Clear pricing/offers for a dedicated capacity commitment

2) Stakeholder mapping (as discussed)
- Alex Turner – Product lead / primary champion (owns feature requirements)
- Priya Singh – Head of Security (owns SOC 2 checklist & evidence)
- Tom Reynolds – Procurement (contracts, SOW, PO)
- Economic buyer TBD — you mentioned this is typically the VP of Engineering or CTO; we'll follow up to confirm.

3) Next steps (I’ll take these actions):
- Share the SOC 2 report, pen test summary, and a sample of audit logs by EOD Monday (Jul 20). (attachment: Redwood-SOC2-report-2025.pdf, pdf)
- Draft a mutual action plan and estimated pricing for Dedicated (30–90 day pilot) by Wednesday.
- Coordinate a short meeting with Priya to walk through security controls / evidence.

Please reply with any corrections to the stakeholder list or additional items to surface for procurement.

Thanks —

Thanks Ben — useful summary. A couple of clarifications from my side:

- Economic buyer: confirm likely to be Leanne Ortiz (VP Engineering). I’ll loop her into procurement conversations once we have the SOC evidence.
- Procurement checklist: we require SOC 2, latest pen test summary, data retention policy, audit logging samples, and a short architecture diagram showing data flows for PII/Risk scope.
- Timeline: security review typically takes 7–10 business days after we receive all artifacts.

Can you indicate whether the pen test was performed by a third party and the date of the engagement? Also need an answer on whether Redwood retains any raw customer inputs longer than 30 days by default (we want explicit retention windows).

Thanks —
